chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, some people narrated from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he prayed four rak'ahs after Friday prayer without separating them with a taslim (salutation).' He said: 'O Zurarah, the Commander of the Faithful prayed behind a faqir (pious person). When he finished and turned away, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) stood up and prayed four rak'ahs without separating them with a taslim. A man beside him said to him: O Abu al-Hasan, you have prayed four rak'ahs without separating them with a taslim. He said:

key_terms.تَسْلِيمٍ: Taslim (salutation ending prayer or separating units)
key_terms.فَاسِقٍ: Pious person (in this context, one who is righteous)

ai.seo_question: Did the Commander of the Faithful separate his post-Friday prayer prayers with taslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential nuance of *salat al-jumu'ah* by illustrating Imam Ali’s flexibility in combining four rak'ahs without a *taslim* when praying behind a just leader, contrasting with the standard two-rak'ah Friday prayer. The description of these as 'similar rak'ahs' (*mushabbahat*) suggests they were treated as a continuous unit of voluntary or extended prayer, reflecting the early Shia emphasis on the Imam’s authority to adapt ritual forms based on context. This incident serves as a key evidence for the permissibility of varying prayer structures in the presence of legitimate leadership.
